title: Four queens: how many tries?
hook: 256 ways to put one queen in each row. How many must you try?

knows: backing up from a dead end in a maze (maze-depth-first)
a chess queen attacks along rows, columns and diagonals (shown on the stage)
doesNotKnow: how much backing up early saves

misconception: Solving a placement puzzle means checking every arrangement.
objective: The learner can explain that placing queens only on safe squares and backing up at a dead row finds both 4-queens solutions in 16 placements instead of checking 256 boards, because a clash cuts off every board that starts that way; and that the saving grows with size.

claims.text: There are 256 boards with one queen in each row of a 4 x 4 board.
claims.source: 4 choices of column in each of 4 rows: 4^4 = 256. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): 4^4 = 256.

claims.text: A full backtracking search from an empty 4 x 4 board (first safe column, back up at a dead row) makes 16 safe placements ('tries'), finds the first solution at try 8, and finds both solutions; the reveal quotes the count and first-solution try from the learner's own finished run.
claims.source: Re-run of step() from Demo.tsx v3 on 2026-10-14: 17 steps, count 16, first solution at 8, solutions columns 2-4-1-3 and 3-1-4-2. | Builder's node script (scratchpad checks/all.mjs), counting each placement of a queen on a square not attacked by the queens above: 16 total, 8 at the first solution, 2 solutions (columns 2 4 1 3 and 3 1 4 2). The stage's Run button uses the same rule and shows the counts. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Own DFS and a copy of the stage's step(): 16 placements, first solution at 8, solutions 2 4 1 3 and 3 1 4 2. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check.

claims.text: Placing only on safe squares notices a clash the moment it happens (the × marks on attacked squares), so every board that starts that way is skipped at once.
claims.source: A partial placement with a conflict cannot be extended to a solution; refusing it removes all 4^(rows left) completions in one step. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): A conflicting prefix has no conflict-free extension; refusing it skips all 4^(rows left) completions. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check.

claims.text: Backtracking makes 2,056 placements to find all 92 solutions of 8 queens.
claims.source: Builder's node script with the same counting rule as the stage (one queen per row, safe squares only, all solutions): 2,056 placements, 92 solutions. 92 also in Wirth, 'Program development by stepwise refinement', CACM 14 (1971). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 10): Own DFS, same counting rule: 2,056 placements, 92 solutions (2,057 nodes with the root). 92: Wirth, CACM 14(4) (1971).

claims.text: That the 4-queens search takes 16 tries, the same as the board's 16 squares, is a coincidence (8 queens: 64 squares but 2,056 placements).
claims.source: Follows from c2 and c5: the placement count is not tied to the square count. Reveal paragraph 2 of Demo.tsx. | Added 2026-10-14 (v3) by demo-builder.

recall.question: A search places items one at a time and stops extending any partial answer the moment it breaks a rule. Why is it so much faster than checking every complete arrangement?
options: It checks the arrangements in a better order
One early clash rules out every arrangement that starts that way
It only works when there is one solution
recall.why: Backing up at the first clash skips all its completions at once: 16 placements instead of 256 boards for 4 queens, 2,056 instead of 16,777,216 for 8.
